letter.subject: Concerns regarding cookie and tracking practices on matthey.com
letter.body:
Dear Data Protection Officer,

I am writing to raise concerns identified during an automated, passive audit of https://matthey.com on 2026-11-08 04:11 UTC. Using a fresh browser, the audit detected the cookie banner, clicked “Reject All”, browsed several public pages, and recorded what was still stored or sent.

The audit found the following:

1. Google cookies were set before any choice was made on the cookie banner. Four cookies were already set before the banner was answered: VISITOR_INFO1_LIVE, VISITOR_PRIVACY_METADATA, YSC and __Secure-YNID. VISITOR_INFO1_LIVE, YSC and __Secure-YNID appeared to hold unique identifiers.

2. Google still received data after cookies were rejected. After “Reject All” was clicked, 70 requests were still sent to google-analytics.com, googlesyndication.com, googletagmanager.com and youtube.com.

3. Scripts from google.com used WebGL GPU-model fingerprinting before any choice was made on the cookie banner. The observed script was loaded from https://www.google.com/js/th/n_BHgtbTP3l_ff810bu_K6lL5wb_ZK3aoRJMIVk8Tks.js.

4. The privacy policy reviewed does not appear to name Google, although Google was observed receiving data. The policy reviewed was https://matthey.com/documents/161599/348554/Job+Applicant+and+Candidate+Privacy+Notice+-+English_China_vr1JM.pdf/ae547f5c-98b3-35dd-d1e8-9738a045226c?t=1661418980792.

5. Our review suggests the privacy notice provided does not cover public website tracking. It is expressly for job applicants and candidates, and states: “本隐私声明适用于寻求 Johnson Matthey 雇佣（或其他服务）机会的任何个人，包括求职者和候选人。” In light of the observed Google tracking on the public website, this appears not to explain the tracking purposes, recipients, legal basis or international transfers for ordinary site visitors.

Please would you:

1. Explain each of the points above.
2. Confirm which cookies and trackers you consider strictly necessary or otherwise exempt, and why.
3. Stop any non-essential cookies, tracking or device-access technologies unless and until valid consent has been obtained.
4. Provide your response within one month.

If this matter is not resolved, it may be raised with the Information Commissioner’s Office.

Yours faithfully,
Joshua Baker

ai_review.summary: The audit shows serious consent-related tracking concerns already identified by the automated checks, including Google identifiers and requests before consent and after rejection. In addition, the supplied privacy notice is recruitment-specific and does not transparently explain the tracking observed on the public website. A separate, applicable website privacy notice may exist, so the additional transparency finding is rated medium.
